output.brief: Pellacott's 2026 VA-220 valves are the problem, not the installers or the firmware. The quality lab found 11% of unused 2026 Pellacott valves leaking at the seat, against 1 in 100 for 2025 Pellacott valves and 0 in 100 for Durrant-Hale. Claim rates for Pellacott valves are the same across new and legacy installers and across firmware 4.1 and 4.2. Durrant-Hale valves stay low in every group. The calibration contractor found Pellacott's VA-220 leak-test rig out of service since January 2026, with no VA-220 test program on any other rig. The per-piece tables in 31 of 36 certificates repeat four fixed sequences, some already used in November 2025. So the certificates do not reflect real tests, and that is why the score rose. I'm fairly confident, about 85%. What to do: do not release the six held lots on new certificates. Quarantine 2026-built Pellacott stock, suspend dock-to-stock, and run Brenmoor's own helium testing before release. Drop the installer remediation and chargebacks. Lock in the supplier's records and notify Pellacott formally. Check other suppliers' records, since that is still unestablished. Reverting to the Ferrand seal is plausible, but the seal and Line 3 can't be separated yet, so test that first. Plan a line-stoppage workaround, such as Durrant-Hale supply.
